title: localStorage
body:
A key-value store in the browser, scoped to an [[Origin]], holding strings, persisting indefinitely until explicitly cleared. Accessed with `localStorage.setItem(key, value)`, `getItem`, `removeItem`. In the venue analogy it's a locker only you can open — and crucially, one you have to open deliberately.

The interview-relevant contrast with [[Cookies]]: localStorage is **never sent to the server automatically**. Nothing attaches it to a request; if the server needs the value, your JS must read it and put it in the request explicitly. That means no direct [[CSRF]] risk, but it also means a token stored here is readable by any JS running on your page, making it a juicier [[XSS]] target than an `HttpOnly` cookie. Capacity is a few megabytes, versus roughly 4KB for a cookie. Compare [[sessionStorage]].
